title: Eclipse moveset file
description: Tune and fork native moves without Lua. Reference: https://dawc17.github.io/ProjectEclipse/api/movesets/

name.description: Label for people reading the file.

move.description: Exact, case-sensitive native move name (or, for a fork, the move to copy).

note.description: Free text for people; kept by the Moveset Lab.

disable.description: true makes the move unselectable. Must be the only change.

expected.description: The value the base game has now. The mod fails to load if it differs.
The value the base game has now. The mod fails to load if it differs.
Current .bytes clip.

asset.description: Binary asset path in this mod, e.g. animations/my_clip.

input.description: The move's key input: expected is the base game's, value the new one.

expected.description: The input the base game has now. The mod fails to load if it differs. One tapped key name, or an array of alternative chords (any one starts the move); each chord is 1-14 keys pressed together. [] is no input.

items.description: A key name (tapped) or { key, press }.

press.description: Tap (default), Hold (keep held) or Release (let go).

value.description: The new input. One tapped key name, or an array of alternative chords (any one starts the move); each chord is 1-14 keys pressed together. [] is no input.

press.description: Tap (default), Hold (keep held) or Release (let go).

select.description: Selects one existing non-attack interval exactly.

type.description: The interval Type, such as Block. Omit when it has none.

name.description: The interval Name, such as Uninterrupt. Omit when it has none.

end.description: Its end frame. Omit to select an open-ended interval.

name.description: Name of the new interval; required without a type.

end.description: Omit for an interval that runs to the end of the move.

id.description: The attack interval ID (usually 0 for the first attack).

value.description: The new [first, last]; last must be after first and inside the clip.

chains.description: Combo links: moves this move may start out of, on its own input, during a window of their keyframes, even where they normally cannot be interrupted.

start.description: First keyframe of the window, in the followed move.

end.description: Last keyframe of the window, in the followed move.
